## 1) Multiple Alleles, Dominance, Incomplete Dominance

> [!recall-yellow]- Q1. Multiple alleles ke case me ek diploid individual me kitni alleles hoti hain?
> **Answer:** Ek diploid individual me kisi bhi gene ki **sirf 2 alleles** hoti hain, chahe population me us gene ke **2 se zyada allelic forms** present hon.
> **Example:** ABO blood group system me population level par multiple alleles hote hain (`Iᴬ`, `Iᴮ`, `i`), lekin ek individual me ek time par sirf **do** hi alleles hongi.

> [!recall-green]- Q2. Pea plant me axial flower aur terminal flower me kaunsa dominant hota hai?
> **Answer:** **Axial** flower position dominant hoti hai, jabki **terminal** recessive hoti hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q3. Violet aur white flower colour me kaunsa dominant hota hai?
> **Answer:** **Violet** flower colour dominant hota hai aur **white** recessive hota hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q4. Law of Dominance kya explain karta hai?
> **Answer:** Law of Dominance yeh explain karta hai ki **F₁ generation me sirf dominant trait express hota hai**, recessive trait mask ho jata hai.
> **Strict NCERT view:** F₁ me dominant trait ka expression **Law of Dominance** se explain hota hai, jabki **F₂ me 3:1 phenotypic ratio** ka basis **Law of Segregation** se better explain hota hai.

> [!recall-red]- Q5. Incomplete dominance Mendel ke kis law ko follow karta hai?
> **Answer:** Incomplete dominance **Law of Segregation** ko follow karta hai, lekin **Law of Dominance** ko नहीं follow karta, kyunki F₁ me koi ek trait poori tarah dominant nahi hota.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q6. Functional point of view se dominant allele kaunsi hoti hai: modified ya unmodified?
> **Answer:** Aksar **unmodified / normal functional allele** dominant hoti hai, kyunki woh proper functional protein ya enzyme banati hai.

> [!recall-red]- Q7. Kya saari modified alleles recessive hoti hain?
> **Answer:** **Nahi.** Har modified allele recessive nahi hoti.
> Generally woh mutations recessive hoti hain jahan gene product **non-functional** ho ya **enzyme na bane**. Lekin kuch mutations dominant bhi ho sakti hain.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q8. Test cross aur back cross me kya difference hota hai?
> **Answer:**
> - **Test cross:** Unknown genotype wale individual ko **homozygous recessive parent** se cross karte hain.
> - **Back cross:** F₁ ko **kisi bhi ek parent** se cross karte hain.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q9. Incomplete dominance me F₁ generation kis jaisi hoti hai? Codominance me kya hota hai?
> **Answer:**
> - **Incomplete dominance:** F₁ phenotype **dono parents ke beech ka intermediate** hota hai.
> - **Codominance:** F₁ me **dono parental traits saath-saath express** hote hain.

## 2) Codominance, ABO Blood Group, Multiple Alleles

> [!recall-green]- Q10. Kaunsa blood group codominance ka classic example hai?
> **Answer:** **AB blood group** codominance ka classic example hai, kyunki `Iᴬ` aur `Iᴮ` dono alleles ek saath express hoti hain.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q11. ABO blood group system me kaunsi alleles sugar polymers banati hain?
> **Answer:** **`Iᴬ` aur `Iᴮ`** alleles RBC surface par **different sugar polymers / antigens** banati hain.
> `i` allele functional antigen nahi banati.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q12. ABO blood group system me kitne phenotypes aur kitne genotypes hote hain?
> **Answer:**
> - **Phenotypes:** 4 → A, B, AB, O
> - **Genotypes:** 6 → `IᴬIᴬ`, `Iᴬi`, `IᴮIᴮ`, `Iᴮi`, `IᴬIᴮ`, `ii`

> [!recall-yellow]- Q13. Multiple alleles ko individual level par study karte hain ya population level par?
> **Answer:** Multiple alleles ko **population level** par study kiya jata hai, individual level par nahi.
> Reason: Population me ek gene ke 2 se zyada allelic forms ho sakte hain, lekin ek diploid individual me sirf 2 alleles hoti hain.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q14. Multiple alleles ka locus same hota hai ya different?
> **Answer:** Multiple alleles **same gene ke alternative forms** hoti hain, isliye unka **locus same hota hai** aur woh **homologous chromosomes ke corresponding position** par milti hain.

## 3) Pleiotropy, Starch Synthesis Gene, Amino Acids

> [!recall-yellow]- Q15. Starch synthesis gene (pea seed example) dominance aur incomplete dominance dono ka example kaise hai?
> **Answer:** Pea me starch synthesis gene seed characteristics ko affect karti hai:
> - **Seed shape** ke level par yeh **dominance** show karti hai.
> - **Starch grain size / biochemical effect** ke level par yeh **incomplete dominance** show kar sakti hai.
> Yeh example dikhata hai ki same gene ka effect phenotype ke different levels par alag tareeke se dikhaai de sakta hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q16. Pleiotropy ka NCERT example kaunsa hai?
> **Answer:** **Phenylketonuria (PKU)** pleiotropy ka important example hai. Isme ek gene mutation multiple phenotypic effects cause karti hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q17. Phenylketonuria me kaunsa enzyme absent ya non-functional hota hai? Kaunsa conversion nahi hota?
> **Answer:* PKU me **phenylalanine hydroxylase** enzyme absent ya non-functional hota hai. Is wajah se **phenylalanine → tyrosine** conversion nahi ho pata.

> [!recall-red]- Q18. Tyrosine essential amino acid hai ya non-essential? Phenylalanine ka kya status hai?
> **Answer:**
> - **Tyrosine:** Normally **non-essential** amino acid
> - **Phenylalanine:** **Essential** amino acid
>
> PKU me phenylalanine se tyrosine nahi ban paati, isliye problem aur serious ho jaati hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q19. Basic aur acidic amino acids ke examples kaun se hain?
> **Answer:**
> - **Basic amino acids:** Lysine, Arginine, Histidine
> - **Acidic amino acids:** Aspartic acid, Glutamic acid

## 4) Sex Determination and Sex-linked Traits

> [!recall-yellow]- Q20. Kaunsa sex determination type aisa hai jahan male me ek chromosome kam hota hai?
 **Answer:** Yeh **XO type sex determination** hota hai.  
> Isme female = **XX** aur male = **XO** hota hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q21. XO type sex determination kahan milta hai?
> **Answer:** XO type sex determination **many insects**, especially **grasshopper**, me milta hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q22. Humans aur Drosophila me kaunsa sex determination system hota hai?
> **Answer:** Humans aur Drosophila dono me **XX-XY type** sex determination hota hai.
> Female = **XX**, Male = **XY**.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q23. Kaunsa sex determination system female heterogamety dikhata hai?
> **Answer:** **ZW-ZZ system** me female heterogametic hoti hai.
> Female = **ZW**, Male = **ZZ**.

> [!recall-green]- Q24. ZW-ZZ system kahan milta hai?
> **Answer:** Yeh system **birds** me milta hai.

> [!recall-red]- Q25. Drosophila me body colour aur eye colour ke genes ke beech recombination frequency kitni hoti hai?
> **Answer:** Drosophila ke tightly linked X-linked traits, especially **yellow body** aur **white eye**, ke beech recombination frequency approximately **1.3%** hoti hai.
> Iska matlab inke beech distance lagbhag **1.3 centiMorgan** hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q26. Drosophila ke yellow body aur white eye genes kis chromosome par hote hain?
> **Answer:** Yeh genes **X chromosome** par hote hain, isliye yeh **X-linked traits** hain.

> [!recall-green]- Q27. Kaun kaun si traits X-linked examples ke roop me yaad rakh sakte hain?
> **Answer:**
> **Drosophila examples:**
> - White eye
> - Yellow body
> - Miniature wing
>
> **Human examples:**
> - Colour blindness
> - Haemophilia

> [!recall-yellow]- Q28. Agar X-linked trait ke liye female homozygous affected ho, to sons me trait kitne percent jayega?
> **Answer:** Agar female **homozygous affected** hai, to uske **100% sons affected** honge, kyunki har son ko apna X chromosome mother se hi milta hai.

## 5) Chromosomal Theory, Linkage, Recombination

> [!recall-yellow]- Q29. Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance kisne di aur kis year me di?
> **Answer:** **Sutton and Boveri** ne **1902** me Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance propose ki.

> [!recall-green]- Q30. Chromosomal Theory of Inheritance ka experimental verification kisne kiya?
> **Answer:** Iska experimental verification **Thomas Hunt Morgan (T. H. Morgan)** ne kiya.

> [!recall-green]- Q31. Drosophila melanogaster ki life cycle lagbhag kitni hoti hai?
> **Answer:** Drosophila ki life cycle lagbhag **2 weeks** hoti hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q32. Linkage parental combinations se kaise related hota hai?
> **Answer:** Linkage **directly proportional** hota hai **parental combinations** se.
> Jitna strong linkage hoga, utne zyada parental combinations milenge.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q33. Gene distance badhne par recombinant frequency par kya effect padta hai?
> **Answer:** Jitna zyada **distance** hoga, उतना zyada **crossing over** ka chance hoga, aur utne hi zyada **recombinants** milenge.

> [!recall-green]- Q34. Morgan ke student ne linkage map banaya tha — unka naam kya tha?
> **Answer:** Morgan ke student **Alfred Sturtevant** ne linkage map banaya tha.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q35. Linkage map ka use Human Genome Project me kis sense me useful tha?
> **Answer:** Linkage maps ne gene mapping ke liye **starting framework** diya. Inse yeh idea milta hai ki genes chromosome par **relative positions** me kahan present ho sakti hain.

> [!recall-red]- Q36. Drosophila me 37.2% recombination kis gene pair ke beech report ki gayi thi?
> **Answer:** **White eye** aur **miniature wing** ke beech approximately **37.2% recombination** observe ki gayi thi.

## 6) Mutation, Chromosomal Aberration, Pedigree, Aneuploidy

> [!recall-yellow]- Q37. Kaunsi mutation me chromosome segment ek non-homologous chromosome par transfer ho jata hai?
> **Answer:** Is type ki mutation ko **translocation** kehte hain.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q38. Cancer ka major chromosomal cause kya maana jata hai?
> **Answer:** **Chromosomal aberrations** cancer ke important causes me se ek hoti hain.

> [!recall-red]- Q39. Agar pedigree me dono parents affected hon aur child normal ho, to kaunsa inheritance pattern sabse likely hai?
> **Answer:** Sabse likely pattern **autosomal dominant** hoga, kyunki affected heterozygous parents (`Aa × Aa`) se normal child (`aa`) aa sakta hai.
> **Important:** Aisa pattern **autosomal recessive** ke saath fit nahi baithta.

> [!recall-green]- Q40. Aneuploidy ka main reason kya hota hai?
> **Answer:** Aneuploidy ka main reason **non-disjunction** hota hai, yani meiosis ke dauraan chromosomes ya chromatids ka sahi tarah separate na hona.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q41. Human me nullisomy ho to total chromosomes kitne honge?
> **Answer:** Human me normal chromosome number **46** hota hai.
> **Nullisomy = 2n − 2**, isliye total chromosome number **44** hoga.

> [!recall-red]- Q42. Double trisomy me total chromosome number kitna hota hai?
> **Answer:** **Double trisomy = 2n + 1 + 1 = 2n + 2**
> Human me total chromosome number **48** hoga.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q43. Autosomal trisomy ke common examples kaun se hain?
> **Answer:**
> - **Down syndrome** → Trisomy 21
> - **Edward syndrome** → Trisomy 18
> - **Patau syndrome** → Trisomy 13

---

## 7) Hardy-Weinberg Principle

> [!recall-green]- Q44. Hardy-Weinberg principle me p aur q kya represent karte hain?
> **Answer:**
> - **p** = dominant allele ki frequency
> - **q** = recessive allele ki frequency
> Aur equation hoti hai:
> **p + q = 1**
> **p² + 2pq + q² = 1**

> [!recall-yellow]- Q45. Agar recessive homozygous genotype ki frequency q² = 0.16 ho, to p, q aur 2pq kitne honge?
> **Answer:**
> - `q² = 0.16`
> - `q = √0.16 = 0.4`
> - `p = 1 - q = 0.6`
> - `2pq = 2 × 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.48`
>
> So final values:
> **q = 0.4**, **p = 0.6**, **2pq = 0.48**

> [!recall-red]- Q46. Agar p² + 2pq = 0.51 ho, to p aur q kaise nikalenge?
> **Answer:**
> Hum jaante hain:
> `p² + 2pq + q² = 1`
> Agar `p² + 2pq = 0.51`, to
> `q² = 1 - 0.51 = 0.49`
> `q = 0.7`
> `p = 0.3`

## 8) Thalassemia and Sickle-cell Anaemia

> [!recall-red]- Q47. HBA genes aur HBB gene kin chromosomes par milte hain?
> **Answer:**
> - **HBA1** aur **HBA2** genes → **Chromosome 16**
> - **HBB** gene → **Chromosome 11**

> [!recall-yellow]- Q48. Thalassemia quantitative disorder hai ya qualitative?
> **Answer:** **Thalassemia** ek **quantitative disorder** hai, kyunki isme globin chain ki **synthesis kam** hoti hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q49. Sickle-cell anaemia quantitative disorder hai ya qualitative?
> **Answer:** **Sickle-cell anaemia** ek **qualitative disorder** hai, kyunki isme globin chain ki **structure abnormal** ho jaati hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q50. Abnormal beta-chain kis disease me banti hai: thalassemia ya sickle-cell anaemia?
> **Answer:** **Sickle-cell anaemia** me **abnormal β-chain** banti hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q51. Beta-chain ki reduced synthesis kis disease me hoti hai?
> **Answer:** **Thalassemia** me β-chain ki **less synthesis** hoti hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q52. Kya HBA1 aur HBA2 closely linked hote hain?
> **Answer:** Haan, **HBA1 aur HBA2 closely linked genes** hain.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q53. Sickle-cell anaemia me mRNA codon level par kya change hota hai?
> **Answer:** mRNA codon **GAG → GUG** me change ho jata hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q54. Sickle-cell anaemia me kaunsa amino acid kis se replace hota hai?
> **Answer:** **Glutamic acid** ki jagah **valine** aa jata hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q55. Valine aur glutamic acid me se kaunsa hydrophobic hota hai?
> **Answer:** **Valine** hydrophobic amino acid hai, jabki **glutamic acid** acidic aur hydrophilic nature dikhata hai.

---

## 9) Polyploidy and Polygenic Inheritance
 
> [!recall-green]- Q56. Polyploidy induce karne ke liye kaunsa chemical use kiya jata hai?
> **Answer:** **Colchicine** polyploidy induce karne ke liye use ki jati hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q57. Polygenic inheritance qualitative hota hai ya quantitative?
> **Answer:** **Polygenic inheritance quantitative** hota hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q58. Polygenic inheritance me major contribution kis allele type ka hota hai?
> **Answer:** Polygenic inheritance me **dominant alleles ka additive contribution** hota hai.

> [!recall-green]- Q59. Polygenic inheritance me environment ka role hota hai kya?
> **Answer:** Haan, **environment bhi contribution deta hai**.
> Isliye quantitative traits me phenotype genes + environment dono par depend karta hai.

> [!recall-red]- Q60. Human skin colour ke polygenic inheritance me kitne loci aur kitni alleles involved maani jaati hain?
> **Answer:** NCERT model ke according:
> - **3 gene pairs / 3 loci** involved hote hain
> - Total **6 alleles** consider ki jaati hain

> [!recall-red]- Q61. Human skin colour me total kitne phenotypic classes possible hoti hain?
> **Answer:** **7 phenotypic classes** possible hoti hain, kyunki 0 se 6 dominant alleles tak additive effect mil sakta hai.

---

## 10) Non-Mendelian Inheritance Patterns

> [!recall-red]- Q62. Kaunsa non-Mendelian pattern F₂ me phenotypic ratio aur genotypic ratio ko same kar deta hai?
> **Answer:** **Incomplete dominance** me F₂ generation me **phenotypic ratio = genotypic ratio = 1 : 2 : 1** hota hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q63. Incomplete dominance ke common examples kaun se hain?
> **Answer:**
> - **Antirrhinum majus** (Snapdragon)
> - **Mirabilis jalapa**

---

## 11) Mendel, Variation, Historical Facts

> [!recall-yellow]- Q64. Chromosomal theory of inheritance segregation-based interpretation se kis scientist ka naam strongly associated hai?
> **Answer:** **Walter Sutton** ne meiosis aur chromosome behaviour ko Mendelian segregation se relate karne me important role play kiya tha. Boveri ke saath milkar unhone chromosomal theory ko strengthen kiya.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q65. Mendel ne kis type ki variation ko study kiya tha — continuous ya discontinuous?
> **Answer:** Mendel ne **discontinuous variation** ko study kiya tha.
> Traits clearly contrasting the, jaise tall vs dwarf, violet vs white.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q66. Mendel ke work ki major limitation kya thi?
> **Answer:** Mendel hereditary factors ke **physical basis** ko explain nahi kar paaye the. Unhe yeh nahi pata tha ki genes actually **chromosomes par physically located** hoti hain.

> [!recall-red]- Q67. Mendel ne apne experiments kis period me kiye the?
> **Answer:** Mendel ne pea plant experiments approximately **1856 se 1863** ke beech kiye the.

> [!recall-red]- Q68. Mendel ne apna kaam kab present aur publish kiya tha?
> **Answer:**
> - **Presented:** 1865
> - **Published:** 1866
>
> Exam me kabhi-kabhi 1865 bhi poocha ja sakta hai, isliye dono yaad rakhna useful hai.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q69. Mendel ke experiments me F₁ generation kis process ka result thi?
> **Answer:** **F₁ generation cross-pollination** ka result thi.

> [!recall-yellow]- Q70. F₂, F₃, F₄ generations kis process ka result thi?
> **Answer:** **F₂, F₃, F₄ generations selfing / self-pollination** ka result thi.

## 12) Rapid Revision Box

> [!recall-yellow]- Q71. 10 ultra-fast recall points ek jagah?
> **Answer:**
> 1. Multiple alleles → population level; individual me sirf 2 alleles
> 2. Axial dominant over terminal
> 3. Violet dominant over white
> 4. Incomplete dominance → F₁ intermediate
> 5. Codominance → AB blood group
> 6. ABO → 4 phenotypes, 6 genotypes
> 7. XO in grasshopper; XY in humans; ZW in birds
> 8. Chromosomal theory → Sutton & Boveri (1902); verification → T. H. Morgan
> 9. Thalassemia quantitative; sickle-cell qualitative
> 10. Polygenic inheritance quantitative + environment affected
